title: Maple-Dijon Brussels Sprouts & Crispy Chickpeas
description: Air-fried Brussels sprouts, chickpeas and red onion tossed in an oil-free maple-Dijon glaze and topped with salted pumpkin seeds.
ingredients: 1 can (540 mL) chickpeas, drained, rinsed and patted dry (about 370g drained)
454g (1 lb) Brussels sprouts, trimmed and quartered
1 small red onion (about 70g), cut into wedges
1 tbsp canola or extra virgin olive oil, divided
instructions: Pat the 370g drained chickpeas very dry with a towel. Leftover moisture keeps them from crisping.
In a large bowl, toss the chickpeas with 1 tsp of the oil and 1/4 tsp smoked paprika. Tip them into the air fryer basket and air-fry at 400°F for 5 minutes.

While the chickpeas cook, add the 454g quartered Brussels sprouts and 70g red onion wedges to the same bowl. Toss them with the remaining 2 tsp oil, the remaining 1/4 tsp smoked paprika and a pinch of black pepper. Leave out the salt for now.

Add the sprouts and onion to the basket with the chickpeas. Air-fry everything at 400°F for 18-20 minutes more, shaking the basket every 6-7 minutes, until the sprouts are charred at the edges and the chickpeas are crisp. If it doesn't all fit in one layer, cook it in 2 batches.
While it cooks, whisk 3 tbsp Dijon mustard, 2 tbsp maple syrup and 1 tsp apple cider vinegar in a small bowl. If the glaze is too thick to coat everything, thin it with 1-2 tsp water.
Move the hot vegetables and chickpeas back to the large bowl and toss them in the whole maple-Dijon glaze until coated.
Taste and add salt only if needed. The Dijon and seeds already bring plenty of salt.
Divide into 4 servings and scatter the 2 tbsp salted pumpkin seeds on top, about 1.5 tsp per serving, just before eating.
notes: Changes from the original to save fat: roasting oil cut from 2 tbsp to 1 tbsp, glaze oil (2 tbsp) dropped, maple cut from 3 tbsp to 2 tbsp, and 1/4 cup almonds replaced with 2 tbsp pumpkin seeds. That brings each serving from about 42g fat down to about 9g. The rice base is dropped because this is a side. The Dijon adds about 1,000mg sodium to the batch, so go light on extra salt. For leftovers, store the seeds separately so they stay crunchy, and re-crisp the sprouts and chickpeas at 380°F for 3-4 minutes. The glaze also works brushed on chicken breast.
